title: Miley Cyrus Honors Dolly Parton at Her Wedding to Maxx Morando
excerpt:
Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have married, with a musical tribute honoring Dolly Parton.
The song Love Is Like a Butterfly carried a personal connection into the ceremony.
body_md:
Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have married, and one of the most touching details reported from their celebration involves the memory of Dolly Parton. The Grammy-winning singer honored her late godmother through a musical reference that connects the occasion to a relationship spanning years of family affection and artistic collaboration.

Reports of the couple's plans had circulated in the days before the wedding. Cyrus's stepsister Lily Purcell shared photographs from the rehearsal dinner, and the subsequent account confirmed that Cyrus and Morando had exchanged vows. Not every detail of the private ceremony has been publicly documented, so the reported tribute is best understood without inventing additional scenes or guest reactions.

The tribute centered on Love Is Like a Butterfly, the opening track of Parton's 1974 album of the same name. Its gentle imagery makes the song particularly appropriate for a wedding. In the context of Cyrus's celebration, the musical choice also allowed someone deeply important to her life to remain symbolically present.

Parton and Cyrus shared more than a professional association. Cyrus has affectionately referred to her godmother as Aunt Dolly, and their relationship has been visible in interviews and performances over many years. That history gives the song selection a personal significance beyond a simple preference for a classic country recording.

The two artists collaborated in 2023 on a new version of Cyrus's hit Wrecking Ball, demonstrating how naturally their musical worlds could meet. Cyrus has also honored Parton during other public appearances, including a Hollywood Bowl performance, and has spoken about the depth of her personality beyond the flamboyant public image.

Love Is Like a Butterfly has had its own long cultural life. Parton performed it with Stephen Colbert on The Colbert Report in 2012, decades after its original release. Its reappearance in the wedding story illustrates how an older song can acquire fresh meaning when attached to an intimate milestone.

The central confirmed elements in this account are the marriage and the tribute. Details beyond those reported should remain private or unverified. What emerges is a story about the continuity of affection: Cyrus begins a new chapter with Morando while acknowledging the influence of a musician and family figure whose presence has shaped much of her life.
